review_comments.body: ⚠️ Edge Case: ODPS import still accepts a missing type that export now rejects `validateRequiredODPSFields` checks only `version`, `product`, `product.details`, `name` and `productID`, and `fromODPSType` still maps a null type to null. So importing an ODPS document without `product.details..type` creates or updates a data product with no `dataProductType`. After this change, the next `GET /{id}/odps` or `/odps/yaml` on that product returns 400. The same goes for every existing data product, because `dataProductType` is optional in `dataProduct.json`. The converter now accepts documents it cannot export again. Either have import validation also reject a missing `type`, so both directions enforce the same required field, or keep import lenient and add a round-trip test documenting that such products can no longer be exported. **Require the ODPS type on import too, so both directions enforce the field:** ```` if (details.getName() == null || details.getName().isBlank()) detailMissing.add("name"); if (details.getProductID() == null || details.getProductID().isBlank()) { detailMissing.add("productID"); } if (details.getType() == null) { detailMissing.add("type"); } ```` - [ ] Apply fix Check the box to apply the fix or reply for a change | Was this helpful? React with 👍 / 👎

⚠️ Quality: Unrecorded API rule: ODPS export answers 400 when the type is missing This changes what the public `GET /v1/dataProducts/{id}/odps` and `/odps/yaml` endpoints (and their name-based versions) return. Previously, a data product without a type was exported with no type field. Now the request gets a 400. The UI export action and any external ODPS consumers have to handle this. Defaulting the type or leaving the field out were also possible choices, so this is a judgment call, not a self-evident bug fix. The rule is stated only in the PR description ("Reject missing `dataProductType` in the shared ODPS export converter with a validation error that names the field"). No record in `docs/decisions/` covers ODPS, and the repository squash-merges, so the description never reaches `git log`. The record would say: "ODPS v4.1 export requires `dataProductType`. A data product without one is rejected with 400 naming the field, instead of being exported with no `product.details..type` or a default type." It should also say whether import enforces the same rule. **Add a decision record and cite it at the check:** ```` // ADR:2026-11-26-odps-export-requires-a-data-product-type private static ODPSProductDetails.OdpsType toODPSType(CreateDataProduct.DataProductType t) { if (t == null) { throw new IllegalArgumentException("dataProductType is required for ODPS export"); } ```` - [ ] Apply fix Check the box to apply the fix or reply for a change | Was this helpful?
